findings.rule: A URN names a text; chapter and verse correspondence milestones must not claim more than they cover (URN scope, Versification)
findings.evidence: Chapter milestones carry whole-chapter URNs (bible:psalms/5, 55, 17, 31, 28, 30, 38, 39, 122, 119, 26; ashrei: psalms/84, 144, 115), but each one is closed by a bare chapter terminator after one or two excerpted verses. In this project bible:psalms/5 therefore resolves to 5:8 alone, even though 5:3-4 appear later in the same file outside that scope. Any compile that lists this project in priority.transclusion (as the expanded settings do, ahead of any Tanakh) gets one verse for a whole-chapter request. Only psalms/145 in ashrei.xml really covers its chapter. In addition, the bare <tei:milestone unit="chapter" n="31"/>, n="30" and n="5" (entering_synagogue.xml:39-40) are terminators by rule 3 that close nothing, yet they look like openers.
findings.required_fix: Remove corresp from every chapter milestone that does not span its whole chapter, or drop those chapter milestones: the verse URNs are fully qualified and need no chapter context. Keep chapter 145 in Ashrei. Remove the redundant bare chapter milestones that carry @n.

findings.rule: Kinds of rubric: a description is placed first inside each passage's scope; strict URN use for texts
findings.evidence: Only the first ח׳ and ק׳ are literal description notes (with corresp instruction:role/reader and role/congregation). The other five speaker labels are j:transclude elements targeting urn:x-opensiddur:instruction:role/reader@… and role/congregation@…. Several things follow. Instruction URNs are swappable under priority.instructions, and machzor_expanded-opensiddur-he, which is listed first, realises the same role URNs as 'חזן'/'קהל' Modim headings. Correct output depends on refdb indexing instruction corresp on description notes. And the printed per-line labels become indirections. The corresp uniqueness rule covers only text: URNs, so repeating the role corresp on literal notes is allowed.
findings.required_fix: Replace each of the five j:transclude elements with a literal <tei:note type="description" rend="rashi" xml:lang="he" corresp="urn:x-opensiddur:instruction:role/…"><tei:choice><tei:abbr>ח׳|ק׳</tei:abbr><tei:expan>חזן|קהל</tei:expan></tei:choice></tei:note> right after the corresponding prayer-part milestone.

expanded_recitation_order.status: Order correct. One partly resolved declaration gap and one dependency-robustness issue.

findings.evidence: The entering-synagogue sequence matches the print through edition-independent URNs (bible:psalms/5/8, 55/15/b, prayer:mah_tovu, …, 39/13/shimah, …, 17/6 twice, 26/12), lines 70-88. Minchah order: Ashrei, then Half Kaddish under a minyan conditional (:136-151), then the silent Amidah first (recitation silent=true, repetition=false) with Qedushat Hashem, Hodaah alone, Shalom, Elohai Netzor and Yehi Ratzon, closed by a sibling j:endDeclare (:189). The minyan-gated repetition (silent=false, repetition=true) substitutes Kedushah for Qedushat Hashem, sets Modim and Modim derabbanan concurrently under role/reader and role/congregation description notes, ends at Shalom, and omits the personal closing prayers. j:endDeclare is at :253. Whole Kaddish is in its own minyan conditional after the repetition's declaration (:257-274). No Birkat Kohanim, which is correct for weekday Ashkenazi Minchah. Kaddish targets are bare edition-independent URNs, and the Birnbaum dependency is documented in sourceDesc (:37-40).
As in the guideline finding, the weekday gate's shabbat=false and yom-tov=false are not declared inside it, so inner conditions on those features stay undecided in the undated compile.
